A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DexWM research despite the changed title. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original open-loop prediction experiments, component ablations, simulation task results, and real-robot grasping trials, including Tables 1–4.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds a pretrained-policy comparison, planner sensitivity results, and a manipulation failure breakdown.

M1.justification: The DINOv2/CDiT architecture, keypoint actions, hand-consistency objective, autoregressive prediction, and CEM planning procedure remain unchanged. The robot hand mappings expanded in Section 3.1 were already documented in v1 Appendix C.2.

E1.justification: Both versions use EgoDex, DROID, exploratory RoboCasa data, Lift evaluation, simulated reaching/grasping/placing, and real-robot grasping. The added controls and analyses operate within this existing coverage.

E2.justification: Section 4.5 adds a Diffusion Policy variant pretrained on the same human dataset and then fine-tuned on robot data. The original Diffusion Policy, DexWM without pretraining, NWM*, PEVA*, and Cosmos comparisons remain; newly cited DWM is not evaluated.

E3.justification: v2 adds a human-pretraining control for Diffusion Policy and planner sweeps over 2/5/7/10 iterations and 64/128/256/512 candidate samples, measuring planning time and success. Existing benchmark splits, rollout horizons, success criteria, trial counts, and default planner settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially broadens diagnostic evidence by testing whether pretraining explains the policy comparison, examining planner cost versus success in Figure 11, and categorizing failures across all three simulated tasks in Table 6. Existing component ablations and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seed-based variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added planner study also reports point estimates, without introducing an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 retain their values. New results include 4% average simulation success for human-pretrained Diffusion Policy versus the retained 53% DexWM average, planning times of 38–168 seconds, and Table 6 failure percentages, including 70% object-drop failures for placing.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, losses, planning objectives, and deterministic-model assumption remain substantively unchanged. The added explanation of dynamics and discussion of static scenes do not introduce a new formal result or derivation.

C1.justification: v2 recasts the principal contribution around learning hand-object interaction dynamics, with robotic manipulation as an application. Its conclusion drops v1's explicit claim of a novel hand-consistency loss and credits the combined representations and loss; the main performance and transfer claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds a pretraining-controlled interpretation of the policy gap, explicit failure mechanisms, and limitations concerning static scenes, external agents, and dependence on simulation adaptation. It removes v1's long-horizon/subgoal warning and first-order-planner discussion, while Appendix B replaces the general slowness concern with a measured compute tradeoff.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly discloses parallel planning rollouts across eight H100 GPUs and episode planning times, including the 168-second default. Existing architecture and training details remain; moving hand-mapping explanations into the main text adds no new implementation information.

R1.justification: v2 adds Dexterous World Models (DWM) to the discussion of closely related interaction models and removes Gradient-based Planning with World Models alongside the first-order-planner discussion. Most cited works and comparative positioning remain.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, conclusion, and substantial portions of the methodological and experimental prose are rewritten around interaction modeling. Terminology and headings change, explanations are condensed, and controllability moves from the ablation discussion to open-loop evaluation.

P2.justification: v2 refreshes Figure 1, incorporates the earlier appendix gripper illustration into Figure 3b, relocates the action-transfer and counterfactual figures, and adds planner Figure 11 and failure Table 6. The overall two-column design and most existing visual content remain.

improvement.justification: The pretrained Diffusion Policy control, measured planning costs, and systematic failure breakdown improve assessment of the retained results and practical limitations. The gain is limited because the new policy control lacks detailed training specifications, and the earlier long-horizon/subgoal caveat disappears without evidence that it was resolved. Overall, the additional diagnostic evidence provides a modest net improvement.
